arxiv-2106-12783.title: Azimuthal equatorial flows in spherical coordinates with discontinuous stratification
arxiv-2106-12783.creator: Calin I. Martin
arxiv-2106-12783.description: Abstract We are concerned here with an exact solution to the governing equations for geophysical fluid dynamics in spherical coordinates which incorporates discontinuous fluid stratification. This solution represents a steady, purely–azimuthal equatorial flow with an associated free-surface and an interface separating two fluid regions, each of which having its own continuous distribution of density.

arxiv-2112-13642.title: Extracting knowledge from features with multilevel abstraction
arxiv-2112-13642.creator: Jinhong Lin Zhaoyang Li
arxiv-2112-13642.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation aims at transferring the knowledge from a large teacher model to a small student model with great improvements of the performance of the student model. Therefore, the student network can replace the teacher network to deploy on low-resource devices since the higher performance, lower number of parameters and shorter inference time.

arxiv-2207-03426.title: Generalized Minimizing Movements for the varifold Canham-Helfrich flow
arxiv-2207-03426.creator: Katharina Brazda, Martin Kružík, Ulisse Stefanelli
arxiv-2207-03426.description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Katharina Brazda, Martin Kružík, Ulisse Stefanelli. The gradient flow of the Canham-Helfrich functional is tackled via the Generalized Minimizing Movements approach. We prove the existence of solutions in Wasserstein spaces of varifolds, as well as upper and lower diameter bounds. In the more regular setting of multiply covered C 1 , 1 C^{1,1} surfaces, we provide a Li-Yau-type estimate for the Canham-Helfrich energy and prove the conservation of multiplicity along the evolution. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
49Q10, 49Q20, 49J45, 53C80, 92C10

arxiv-2311-16653.title: Pair creation in hot electrosphere of compact astrophysical objects
arxiv-2311-16653.creator: Mikalai Prakapenia, Gregory Vereshchagin
arxiv-2311-16653.description: Abstract The mechanism of pair creation in electrosphere of compact astrophysical objects such as quark stars or neutron stars is revisited, paying attention to evaporation of electrons and acceleration of electrons and positrons, previously not addressed in the literature. We perform a series of numerical simulations using the Vlasov-Maxwell equations.

arxiv-2401-03044.title: Machine learning inspired models for Hall effects in non-collinear magnets
arxiv-2401-03044.creator: Jonathan Kipp, Fabian R. Lux, Thorben Pürling, Abigail Morrison, Stefan Blügel, Daniele Pinna, Yuriy Mokrousov
arxiv-2401-03044.description: Abstract The anomalous Hall effect has been front and center in solid state research and material science for over a century now, and the complex transport phenomena in nontrivial magnetic textures have gained an increasing amount of attention, both in theoretical and experimental studies.

arxiv-2404-06204.title: Precise measurements of W W - and Z Z -boson transverse momentum spectra with the ATLAS detector using p ​ p pp collisions at s = 5.02 \sqrt{s}=5.02 TeV and 13 13 TeV
arxiv-2404-06204.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2404-06204.description: Abstract This paper describes measurements of the transverse momentum spectra of W W and Z Z bosons produced in proton–proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies of s = 5.02 \sqrt{s}=5.02 TeV and s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider.

arxiv-2509-07063.title: Simulations of Flare Chemistry in Brown Dwarf Companions to Active M Dwarfs Facilities: UCLA Hoffman2 Cluster
arxiv-2509-07063.creator: Aidan Gibbs, Michael P. Fitzgerald
arxiv-2509-07063.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Aidan Gibbs, Michael P. Fitzgerald. Brown dwarfs that are short period ( < 10 <10\, day) companions to actively flaring M dwarfs may provide a context to directly observe flare-driven photochemistry and structural changes in an extrasolar planet-like atmosphere. To assess the viability of directly observing flare impacts in the atmosphere of a brown dwarf, we perform self-consistent temperature-chemistry modeling of the atmospheric response to individual energetic superflares. We modified the existing open-source VULCAN chemical-kinetics and HELIOS radiative-transfer codes for this purpose.

arxiv-2601-14363.title: Chemical evolution of close massive binaries - tidally-enhanced or tidally-suppressed mixing?
arxiv-2601-14363.creator: Luca Sciarini, Sophie Rosu, Sylvia Ekström, Maxime Marchand, Patrick Eggenberger, Georges Meynet
arxiv-2601-14363.description: Abstract Context. One of the largest source of uncertainties in the predictions of stellar models comes from the internal transport mechanisms. In close massive binaries, previous theoretical studies suggest that tides consistently boost chemical mixing. However, observations do not reveal any clear period-nitrogen enrichment trend, challenging these predictions.

pmc-10530390.title: Understanding Key Predictors of Life Satisfaction in a Nationally Representative Sample of Koreans
pmc-10530390.creator: Yun-Kyeung Choi, Mohsen Joshanloo, Jae-Ho Lee, Hong-Seock Lee, Heung-Pyo Lee, Jonghwan Song, Gilbert Ramirez
pmc-10530390.description: The purpose of this study was to examine the factors that predict life satisfaction in a large representative sample of Koreans by analyzing data from the Gallup World Poll. The primary objective was to identify important predictors and suggest strategies to improve quality of life in Korea.

pmc-10642048.title: Epidemiological characteristics of seven notifiable respiratory infectious diseases in the mainland of China: an analysis of national surveillance data from 2017 to 2021
pmc-10642048.creator: Le-le Deng, Ya-jun Han, Zhuo-wei Li, Da-yan Wang, Tao Chen, Xiang Ren, Guang-xue He
pmc-10642048.description: BackgroundRespiratory infectious diseases (RIDs) remain a pressing public health concern, posing a significant threat to the well-being and lives of individuals. This study delves into the incidence of seven primary RIDs during the period 2017–2021, aiming to gain deeper insights into their epidemiological characteristics for the purpose of enhancing control and prevention strategies.

pmc-10698641.title: Advanced fabrication approach for innovative triple base propellants with enhanced continuous fracture resistance†
pmc-10698641.creator: Yao Zhu, You Fu, Bin Xu, Zhitao Liu, Feiyun Chen, Xiaoan Wei, Xin Liao
pmc-10698641.description: This paper initially contrasts the solvent-based and solventless molding processes, subsequently optimizing a sustainable and efficient solventless molding route for both STP and SLTP. Key physicochemical parameters such as extrusion rate, residual volatile solvents, moisture content, and apparent density of both propellant types are meticulously compared.

pmc-10881047.title: ATP1A3 as a target for isolating neuron-specific extracellular vesicles from human brain and biofluids
pmc-10881047.creator: Yang You, Zhengrong Zhang, Nadia Sultana, Maria Ericsson, Yuka A. Martens, Min Sun, Takahisa Kanekiyo, Seiko Ikezu, Scott A. Shaffer, Tsuneya Ikezu
pmc-10881047.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Neuron-derived extracellular vesicles (NDEVs) are potential biomarkers of neurological diseases although their reliable molecular target is not well established. Here, we demonstrate that ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit alpha 3 (ATP1A3) is abundantly expressed in extracellular vesicles (EVs) isolated from induced human neuron, brain, cerebrospinal fluid, and plasma in comparison with the presumed NDEV markers NCAM1 and L1CAM by using super-resolution microscopy and biochemical assessments.

pmc-11352313.title: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte and Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio: Side by Side with Molecular Mutations in Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer—The INOLUNG Study
pmc-11352313.creator: Corina Eugenia Budin, Iuliu Gabriel Cocuz, Liviu Sorin Enache, Ionuț Alexandru Rența, Cristian Cazacu, Dariana Elena Pătrîntașu, Mihai Olteanu, Ruxandra-Mioara Râjnoveanu, Edith Simona Ianoși, Armand Râjnoveanu, Ovidiu Simion Cotoi
pmc-11352313.description: Simple SummaryThis retrospective observational study recruited 380 patients, 115 with lung cancer and 265 in the control group. Both the neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and the platelet/lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were significantly higher in cancer patients than in the control group. The correlation of PLR with the probability of lung cancer differs between men and women.

pmc-11472475.title: The providing multidisciplinary ILD diagnoses (PROMISE) study – study design of the national registry of Japan facilitating interactive online multidisciplinary discussion diagnosis
pmc-11472475.creator: Yasuhiro Kondoh, Taiki Furukawa, Hironao Hozumi, Takafumi Suda, Ryoko Egashira, Takeshi Jokoh, Junya Fukuoka, Masataka Kuwana, Ryo Teramachi, Tomoyuki Fujisawa, Yoshinori Hasegawa, Takashi Ogura, Yasunari Miyazaki, Shintaro Oyama, Satoshi Teramukai, Go Horiguchi, Akari Naito, Yoshikazu Inoue, Kazuya
pmc-11472475.description: BackgroundMultidisciplinary discussion (MDD), in which physicians, radiologists, and pathologists communicate and diagnose together, has been reported to improve diagnostic accuracy compared to diagnoses made solely by physicians. However, even among experts, diagnostic concordance of MDD is not always good, and some patients may not receive a specific diagnosis due to insufficient findings.

pmc-11476790.title: Dengue Envelope Protein as a Cytotoxic Factor Inducing Hemorrhage and Endothelial Cell Death in Mice
pmc-11476790.creator: Te-Sheng Lien, Der-Shan Sun, Wen-Sheng Wu, Hsin-Hou Chang
pmc-11476790.description: Dengue virus (DENV) infection, prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions, can progress to dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF), which increases mortality during secondary infections. DHF is characterized by endothelial damage and vascular leakage. Despite its severity, no specific antiviral treatments exist, and the viral factors responsible for endothelial damage remain unclear.

pmc-11615760.title: Multiplexed SERS Detection of Serum Cardiac Markers Using Plasmonic Metasurfaces
pmc-11615760.creator: Peng Zheng, Lintong Wu, Piyush Raj, Jeong Hee Kim, Santosh Kumar Paidi, Steve Semancik, Ishan Barman
pmc-11615760.description: Surface‐enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) possesses exquisite molecular‐specific properties with single‐molecule sensitivity. Yet, translation of SERS into a quantitative analysis technique remains elusive owing to considerable fluctuation of the SERS intensity, which can be ascribed to the SERS uncertainty principle, a tradeoff between “reproducibility” and “enhancement”.

pmc-12648497.title: Isolation of F-specific Inovirus filamentous phages from environmental sewage samples
pmc-12648497.creator: Natasha Theriault, Bradley W.M. Cook, Steven S. Theriault, Deborah A. Court
pmc-12648497.description: Bacteriophage (phage) isolation from various environmental sources is an important step in identifying phages suitable for therapeutic and/or research purposes. Most published protocols outlining phage isolation techniques focus on the identification and/or characterization of strictly lytic phages. Here, a simple, adapted protocol specific for the isolation of non-lytic, filamentous phages is described.

pmc-13138533.title: Closing the loop on catheter-associated urinary tract infections: A prospective risk assessment and scoring system for the early prediction and prevention of catheter-associated urinary tract infection
pmc-13138533.creator: Rajan Ravichandran, Roshan Yedulla Reddy, Velmurugan Palaniyandi, Hariharasudhan Sekar, Sriram Krishnamoorthy
pmc-13138533.description: Background:Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI) are among the most common healthcare-associated infections, particularly in hospitalised patients requiring prolonged catheterisation. Despite standard protocols, preventable lapses in catheter care and clinical practices contribute to the incidence of these infections.Aims and Objectives:This study aimed to identify significant risk factors and develop a point-based CAUTI Risk Scoring System for early prediction and intervention.

pmc-13433856.title: Clinically interpretable deep learning for breast cancer missense variant pathogenicity prediction
pmc-13433856.creator: Rahaf M. Ahmad, Noura AlDhaheri, Mohd Saberi Mohamad, Bassam R. Ali
pmc-13433856.description: BackgroundMissense variants in breast cancer remain diagnostically challenging due to their functional diversity and complex genomic contexts. Conventional laboratory assays for evaluating pathogenicity are labor-intensive, costly, and often impractical for large-scale screening, creating a pressing need for accurate, scalable, and clinically interpretable computational approaches.
